# Service exit-risk catalog

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen_catalog_doc.py from src/exitrisk/data/service_catalog.yaml (version 2026.10.5). Do not edit by hand. -->

Every AWS service that appears in Cost Explorer is classified into one of five tiers by how much of a workload must change to leave AWS. The tier sets the service's score in the exit-risk calculation; the migration path, equivalents and typical duration are for **one workload** of that service. This is the same content as Appendix A of the generated report.

| Tier | Label | Score | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Portable | 10 | Commodity infrastructure or an open standard. Lift-and-shift; configuration moves, code does not change. |
| 2 | Low | 30 | Managed flavour of an open engine or de-facto standard API. Data and configuration migrate; little code change. |
| 3 | Moderate | 50 | AWS-specific API with a close equivalent on every major cloud. Code changes at the integration points. |
| 4 | High | 75 | Proprietary programming or data model. The workload must be redesigned, not just re-pointed. |
| 5 | Critical | 95 | No equivalent outside AWS. Rebuild, re-platform or replace with a product; often a business change. |

120 services classified. Unknown services score as tier 3 and are flagged on the report's data-quality panel.

**AI agent help** is how much AI coding agents cut a service's engineering weeks when the Exit model says teams use them: high about 50% (code and templates an agent can translate), medium about 25%, low about 10%, none for data moves, hardware, contracts and managed-service redesign.

**Migration tools** are named where tools do part of the move, with their help on the same scale when the Exit model says they will be used (never below 30% of the work together with AI agents).

## Billing lines excluded from scoring

These are not workloads: Tax (Tax on AWS charges; not a workload.), AWS Support (Support plan fee; replaced by the target provider's support contract.), Savings Plans (Commitment fee rather than a workload. Note the commitment term in the exit plan - it is a cost of leaving early.), Billing tools (Billing tooling; not a workload.)
